newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes higher against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes higher against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up slightly at 8.2980 against the U.S. dollar on Monday from last Friday's 8.2984 due to solid bids for the yuan on the Shanghai-based interbank foreign exchange market, traders said.
Traders said demand for the local unit continued to dominate movement, but the yuan's rise was gradual in dull trading.
The yuan opened higher at 8.2980 and moved steadily around the opening level for most of the session, hitting an intra-day low of 8.3028 and a high of 8.2934.
Trading was dull, with most done at about 8.2980, traders said.
"Speculative trading was less apparent today, probably out of fear of intervention by the central bank, even though the trading limits have been widened," one dealer said.
He said business mainly focused on position adjustment in the absense of fresh factors.
"The strong bids for the yuan made its downside solid at about 8.2990 and 8.30." he added.
Dealers expect the yuan to move around 8.2980 on Tuesday.
The yuan closed up at an intra-day high of 7.0650 from 7.2000 against 100 Japanese yen in line with the yen's fall on the world market.
The yuan closed slightly up at an intra-day high of 1.0718 from 1.0720 against the Hong Kong dollar.
